title: Positivity of the Gaussian logarithmic tail scale
statement: Let $\Phi$ be the cumulative distribution function of the standard Gaussian and define $L(t)=2\log(1/\Phi(t))$. Then $L(t)>0$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$.
replaced: Let $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ and $L(t)=2\log(1/\Phi(t))$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. For every real $t$, one has $0<L(t)$.
